ops.title: internal/cli takes 930s under -race and keeps growing
ops.description:
`go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli` measures **930s** (2026-08-03), past Go's
default 10-minute per-package timeout. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and
`Taskfile.yml` now pass `-timeout 30m` so they stay green, but that is a
stopgap: the number grew from ~450s to 930s in one round of conversions and will
keep growing.

The cost is real fixtures, which is the point of the work — but it is not evenly
spread. `vcstest.Repo` runs a real `git init` (~150ms), `jj git init --colocate`
(~500ms), or `gt init` + `gt track` (~2.5s including a mandatory cache drain),
roughly 250 times per run. `t.Parallel()` is unavailable by construction (the
fixture uses `t.Setenv` and `t.Chdir`; Go panics), so the usual mitigation does
not apply.

Options, roughly in order of payoff per unit of work:
1. **Prototype-and-copy in `vcstest`**: build ONE repo per shape and copy the
   tree for each fixture instead of re-running init. Biggest single win, and it
   changes no test.
2. **Share one fixture per non-mutating table** — already the established
   practice, but not applied everywhere; the gt-bearing tables pay the most.
3. **Split the ship suite into its own package** so each package gets its own
   10m budget and the two run concurrently.

Note a trap that hid this: `go test ... | tail` exits 0 even when the package
times out, so a pipeline-wrapped run reports success. Check `${pipestatus[1]}`,
or do not pipe.

ops.text: internal/cli's -race wall time is brought back under Go's 10m default, or the suite is split so each package fits its own budget
